summary: Lafutidine is a second-generation histamine H2-receptor antagonist (used mainly in Japan and parts of Asia) that suppresses gastric acid secretion and also has gastroprotective actions mediated through capsaicin-sensitive afferent neurons and increased gastric mucosal blood flow and mucus/somatostatin. It is used for peptic ulcer disease, gastritis and reflux symptoms. It provides relatively long-lasting acid suppression at low doses. It is not FDA-approved; this record is based on the Japanese package insert/SmPC, BNF-type sources and the H2-antagonist class.
indications: Acute exacerbation of chronic gastritis (gastric mucosal lesions - erosion, bleeding, redness, edema)
Reflux esophagitis / symptomatic gastro-esophageal reflux (per regional labeling)
Pre-anesthetic reduction of gastric acid (per regional labeling)

moa: Lafutidine competitively and reversibly blocks histamine H2 receptors on gastric parietal cells, reducing basal and stimulated gastric acid secretion. In addition to acid suppression it exerts gastroprotective effects via capsaicin-sensitive sensory (afferent) nerves, increasing gastric mucosal blood flow, mucus and bicarbonate secretion and somatostatin, which helps protect and heal the mucosa.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to lafutidine or other H2-receptor antagonists
relative: Elderly or debilitated patients (monitor for CNS/hematologic effects)
monitor: Drugs whose absorption depends on gastric acidity (e.g. azole antifungals, atazanavir)
Patients with cardiac disease (rare arrhythmia reports with H2 blockers)

preg: Safety in pregnancy is not well established; use only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk, in line with general caution for H2-receptor antagonists.
lact: Data on excretion into human milk are limited; H2-antagonists can pass into breast milk. Avoid or use with caution during breastfeeding and weigh the importance of the drug to the mother.
renal: Lafutidine and metabolites are partly renally eliminated; in significant renal impairment consider a reduced dose and monitor, as accumulation may increase the risk of adverse effects.
hepatic: Use with caution in significant hepatic impairment. Rare hepatic enzyme elevations have been reported with H2-antagonists; monitor if clinically indicated.

moderate: pH-dependent drugs (ketoconazole, itraconazole, atazanavir, certain protease inhibitors) - reduced absorption due to higher gastric pH
Other acid-suppressing agents - additive effect, usually unnecessary together
minor: Iron salts, some tyrosine kinase inhibitors - possible reduced absorption at higher gastric pH
Drugs altering renal clearance - theoretical effect on lafutidine elimination
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; no major food interaction.
interactions.alcohol: Limit alcohol, which aggravates acid-related disorders.
interactions.diagnostics: May suppress gastric acid affecting urea breath / gastrin testing; rarely alters CBC or liver enzymes. Stop before testing for Helicobacter pylori as appropriate.

emergency: Severe blood dyscrasia (fever, sore throat, bleeding)

monitoring: Symptom relief and ulcer/esophagitis healing (endoscopy where appropriate)
Exclusion of gastric malignancy in alarm features or persistent symptoms
CBC and liver function on prolonged therapy if clinically indicated
Mental status in elderly or renally impaired patients

pearls: Not FDA-approved; lafutidine is used mainly in Japan and parts of Asia - dosing/indications here follow the Japanese package insert and the H2-antagonist class rather than an FDA label
Second-generation H2 blocker with added gastroprotection via capsaicin-sensitive afferent nerves (increased mucosal blood flow, mucus and somatostatin), not just acid suppression
Provides potent, relatively long-lasting acid suppression at a low (10 mg) dose, particularly useful for nocturnal acid
Acid suppression can mask gastric cancer - exclude malignancy before treating ulcer symptoms
Higher gastric pH can reduce absorption of pH-dependent drugs such as azole antifungals and atazanavir
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember unless it is almost time for the next dose, in which case skip it and resume your usual schedule. Do not take two doses at once.
overdose: Specific overdose data for lafutidine are limited. Based on the H2-antagonist class, overdose is generally well tolerated; possible effects include exaggerated pharmacologic actions and, rarely, CNS effects (confusion) especially with renal impairment. There is no specific antidote; treat supportively with symptomatic care, monitoring, and removal of unabsorbed drug if recent and appropriate.
